purpose: This PR addresses issue #528 with three WP 7.1+ integrations: size-aware encode-quality resolution via wp_get_image_encode_quality() with an LQIP quality guard, migration of preconnect/dns-prefetch emission to core's wp_resource_hints() filter, and an admin toggle overriding WP 7.1+ client-side MIME processing (plus an object-cache wp_cache_supports() feature-claim fix and new PHP/JS tests).
riskRationale: The new ImgConverterTest suite fails outright (2 errors + 5 failures under composer test), and convert_image() now contains two competing quality-resolution blocks — the post-getimagesize block is dead code and would raise a TypeError (array passed to an int parameter) if ever reached, so full-size originals are encoded without the real dimensions core's size-aware API needs. The changed code paths are core to image conversion and resource-hint output, so regressions affect production image quality and page markup, not just tests.
breakingChanges: Preconnect/dns-prefetch links now render via core's wp_resource_hints() with normalization to scheme+host (preconnect) and protocol-relative //host (dns-prefetch); output is functionally equivalent but no longer byte-identical to the legacy echo path.

convert_image() quality resolution changed: sub-sized images now get per-size quality from wp_get_image_encode_quality() instead of the flat wp_image_quality() value, which may change encoded file sizes.
wp_cache_supports() now claims add_multiple, exposing a new feature to core callers on the object-cache drop-in.

text: The PR's intent is sound and well-documented (size-aware encode quality, resource hints via core, client-side MIME override), and the resource-hints and MIME-override work is covered by passing tests. However, the image-quality change is broken in two ways: the new quality resolution is implemented as two blocks where the second (the one using real image dimensions) is unreachable dead code, and the new ImgConverterTest suite fails with 2 errors and 5 failures. Because the required verification gate (composer test) does not pass, the PR is not ready to merge.

reasoning: composer test fails in the newly added ImgConverterTest tests (ReflectionException from invoking a non-static private method with a null receiver, plus 5 assertion failures caused by a dead duplicate quality-resolution block, an always-stubbed wp_get_image_encode_quality(), and cross-test stub pollution). These defects must be fixed and the full verification suite run before merge.

message: Migrating preconnect/dns-prefetch to the wp_resource_hints() filter is idiomatic: it leverages core's batching/deduplication/normalization, preserves the crossorigin='anonymous' attribute via array hints, and normalizes bare-hostname dns-prefetch origins to protocol-relative form so core's host guard does not drop them. Backed by a dedicated passing test suite.

The client_side_supported_mime_types override is well-guarded: the filter is only registered when the WP 7.1+ function exists and the toggle is enabled, non-array stored values degrade gracefully, and the stored selection is sanitized and intersected with core's authoritative list so an unsupported format (e.g. HEIC) can never shadow core.

resolve_encode_quality() correctly guards a null/zero result from wp_get_image_encode_quality() before casting, preventing the classic (int) null encoding-at-quality-0 bug, and the LQIP path is correctly kept on a fixed quality=40 so inline data URIs do not double in size.

convert_image() now contains two duplicate quality-resolution blocks. The block at lines 251-270 runs first (before getimagesize) and always leaves $quality !== -1 (it sets $quality or falls back to 82), so the second block at lines 318-340 — which was clearly intended to be the real resolution using the actual image dimensions — is unreachable dead code. As a result, full-size originals (no -WxH filename suffix) pass an empty size array and the hardcoded 82 to wp_get_image_encode_quality() instead of the real dimensions.
suggestion: Delete the early block (lines 251-270) and keep only the post-getimagesize block, fixing its call signature so the size array is passed as the $size argument and the fallback default is passed separately (make $fallback nullable so core computes its own per-format baseline).

message: The dead second resolution block calls self::resolve_encode_quality( 'image/avif', $size ) and self::resolve_encode_quality( $mime, $size ), passing the $size array where the signature declares int $fallback. This is a latent TypeError (arrays are never coerced to int) that will fatal if the block is ever reached — e.g. when the first block is removed as part of the intended refactor.
suggestion: When consolidating the two blocks, always pass the fallback and size in the correct positions, e.g. resolve_encode_quality( $mime, null, $size ), and use $this-> instead of self:: on this instance method for consistency with the first block.

message: test_resolve_encode_quality_resolves_per_format_quality() and test_resolve_encode_quality_falls_back_to_wp_image_quality() invoke the private non-static method resolve_encode_quality() via $method->invoke( null, ... ), producing 'ReflectionException: Trying to invoke non static method ... without an object'. This is one of the two errors failing the suite.
suggestion: Instantiate the converter first (as the other new tests do via make_converter()) and pass the instance as the receiver instead of null.

message: test_convert_image_uses_wp_get_image_encode_quality() and test_convert_image_webp_uses_wp_get_image_encode_quality() assert the captured args are array('image/avif', array('width'=>64,'height'=>48), null), but the implementation resolves quality before getimagesize from the filename (empty size) and passes 82 as the core default, yielding array('image/avif', array(), 82). The tests encode the intended contract (real dimensions + null default so core computes its baseline); the implementation does not satisfy it, so the tests fail.
suggestion: Consolidate quality resolution to run after getimagesize with the real $image_info dimensions and pass a nullable default to wp_get_image_encode_quality(), then re-run composer test to confirm the captured arguments match the assertions.

message: test_resolve_encode_quality_falls_back_to_flat_core_quality(), test_resolve_encode_quality_falls_back_to_default(), and test_resolve_encode_quality_uses_size_aware_core_helper() fail because setUp() stubs wp_get_image_encode_quality() (justReturn(82)) in every test, so function_exists() is always true and the WP 7.1+ branch is always taken, never exercising the wp_image_quality() or fallback-default branches the tests target. Additionally, test_resolve_encode_quality_falls_back_to_wp_image_quality() (line 504) patches function_exists() and test_resolve_encode_quality_falls_back_to_flat_core_quality() (line ~554) stubs wp_image_quality(), and those stubs leak across tests in the class, causing order-dependent failures.
suggestion: Remove the blanket wp_get_image_encode_quality() stub from setUp() and have each test define only the functions it needs, restoring function_exists()/wp_image_quality() stubs at the end of the tests that patch them (or use dedicated stubs scoped per test) so Brain Monkey state does not leak between tests.

message: The resolve_encode_quality() docblock opens with two consecutive '/**' markers (lines 167-168), a malformed docblock that is silently tolerated by the parser but misdocuments the method.
suggestion: Remove the duplicate '/**' opener so only one docblock start remains.
